_comment: MULTI-HEAD: examples 01, 02 and 03 trained as ONE model.
bulk        64 H2O, 3D-periodic     RPBE-D3          192 atoms
molecules   4 species, no cell      OMol25 DFT       8-32 atoms
slab        Li/LiFSI, 2D-periodic   UMA MLIP         468 atoms
Three things forbid one head here. The boundary treatment differs
(slab correction on / off / no cell at all), the labels come from three
different levels of theory, and the energy zeros are unrelated. What
they CAN share is the descriptor: local geometry is local geometry.
Run step 1 of each of the three examples first -- this file reads their
data/ folders and writes nothing of its own.
shared_dict holds the things more than one branch points at, by name.
A branch writes "descriptor": "backbone" instead of a dict, and every
branch that does gets THE SAME MODULE OBJECT -- not a copy. One set of
weights, updated by whichever branch the step was drawn from.
Only type_map, descriptor and fitting_net can be shared. long_range is
per-branch by construction, which is what lets the boundary treatment
differ.
That is right HERE, where the three branches are three levels of theory
with unrelated energy zeros. When branches share a theory and differ
ONLY in boundary condition, `same_as` ties everything instead -- see
examples/05-pseudo-head.

_comment_type_map_all: ONE type_map for the whole model -- multi-task asserts it.
It used to have to be the hand-computed UNION over all three
examples (H,O from bulk; C,Cl,H,N,O,P,S,Si from the molecules;
C,F,H,Li,N,O,S from the slab), and a missed element failed at load.
With the full periodic table there is no union to get wrong, and a
fourth branch can be added without touching this list at all.
_comment_backbone: The shared DPA4C. rcut 6.0 must stay below half of the SMALLEST cell
in any branch -- bulk water at 12.429 A gives 6.21 A, so 6.0 fits,
but only just. A branch with a smaller cell would force rcut down
for every branch, because there is only one descriptor.
add_chg_spin_ebd is part of DPA4C's structural signature, so it must
be TRUE IN EVERY BRANCH or sharing is refused -- one module cannot
have two shapes. Here it is written once, which makes that automatic.
default_chg_spin is the fallback for the two branches whose data
carries no charge_spin.npy; it is deliberately NOT in the signature.

bulk._comment: Example 01 verbatim, minus the parts now shared.
bulk._comment_data_stat_nbatch: Frames per system used for the output-bias statistics. The default 10 builds a dense neighbour matrix over 10 frames at once -- at 468 atoms that is tens of GiB. It is a MODEL key, per branch, not a training one.

_comment: No cell: the reciprocal sum becomes the direct pair sum. Same

_comment: One loss per branch, keyed by branch name. None of the three has
virial labels, so every prefactor stays 0 -- but a branch that DID
have them could switch them on here without touching the others.
model_prob is the probability a given STEP is drawn from that branch.
It is not a data-size weight: the slab has 30 training frames against
the bulk's 543, so equal weights would revisit each slab frame ~18x
more often. 0.2 already flatters it -- see the README.
_comment_gradient_max_norm: NOT OPTIONAL HERE. Branches push the shared backbone with wildly
different gradient norms -- measured at init: bulk 5.0e9,
molecules 1.9e6, slab 4.8e5. Without clipping the bulk branch
simply overwrites what the others learn. See the README.
